definition_en: firm and not shaking, and continuing at a constant rate
core_image: 一只手稳稳托住不断晃动的梯子
scene: 她扶稳了梯子。She held the ladder steady.
sceneCN: 这里 steady 是「稳固的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她扶稳了梯子。

senses.title: Not shaking
senses.definition: firm and supported so that it does not shake or fall
senses.definitionCN: 牢固支撑而不摇晃、不倒下的
senses.example: She held the ladder steady.
senses.why: This is the physical sense you can see.
senses.whyCN: 这是肉眼可见的物理义项。

senses.title: Constant rate
senses.definition: developing or moving at a regular and unchanging speed
senses.definitionCN: 以规律而不变的速度发展或移动
senses.example: The company showed steady growth.
senses.why: A thing that does not shake also does not jump or drop.
senses.whyCN: 不摇晃的东西，也不会忽起忽落。

senses.title: Calm and reliable
senses.definition: calm, sensible, and dependable in behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 举止冷静、明智而可靠的
senses.example: He is a steady worker.
senses.why: A steady hand became a steady character.
senses.whyCN: 稳定的手，引申为稳定的性格。

intro.en: Steady is built on the old noun stead, a place, with the adjective ending -y.
intro.cn: steady 由古名词 stead（位置）加形容词后缀 -y 构成。

items.en: Stede meant a place or a position.
Stede also named a person's standing.
items.cn: stede 也指一个人的立足之处。

items.en: Steady described something fixed in place.
items.cn: steady 描述固定在原处的东西。

items.en: The sense widened to regular and calm.
items.cn: 词义扩展到规律与沉着。

items.en: A steady job came to mean secure work.
items.cn: 「稳定的工作」逐渐指有保障的职业。

note.en: Steady is compared with look-alike words and with words for firmness.
note.cn: 把 steady 与形近词以及表示稳固的词作比较。

entries.definition: not likely to change or fall

normalIntro.en: Steady means standing in one place, then moving at one pace, then keeping one calm mind.
normalIntro.cn: steady 是站在一个地方不动，接着按一个速度前进，再保持一颗平静的心。

normal.en: Hold the camera steady.
Rain fell at a steady rate.
She has a steady job.
His voice stayed steady.
Slow and steady wins the race.
normal.cn: 稳扎稳打才能赢得比赛。

abstract.en: To stand in one place is already a kind of courage.
abstract.cn: 能在一个地方站住，本身就是一种勇气。

abstract.en: Steadiness is the quiet form of strength.
abstract.cn: 稳定，是力量安静的样子。

abstract.en: A steady hand makes a long journey short.
abstract.cn: 手稳，长路也会变短。

examples.en: She held the ladder steady.
The company showed steady growth.
He is a steady worker.

dict_mnemonic.text: steady 由 stead（位置）加 -y 构成，本义是站稳不动，引申为速度均匀、性格沉稳；steady growth 是稳步增长。

root: 来自古英语 stede（地方、位置），加形容词后缀 -y；由站稳不动引申为匀速发展，再引申为性格沉稳可靠。

sensesIntro.en: Steady describes something that does not shake, does not change pace, and does not lose its calm.
sensesIntro.cn: steady 描述不摇晃、不改变节奏、也不失冷静的事物。

core.en: A hand that does not tremble.

branches.en: A ladder leans and a hand presses it still.
branches.cn: 梯子倾斜，一只手把它按稳。

branches.en: A line on a chart climbs without a jump.
branches.cn: 图表上的线平稳上升，没有跳跃。

branches.en: A voice answers slowly in a crisis.
branches.cn: 危机中，一个声音缓缓作答。

branches.en: What stands firm also moves at an even pace.
branches.cn: 站得稳的东西，前进也匀。

branches.en: Even growth and even temper share one calm.
branches.cn: 平稳的增长与平和的脾气，共享同一种冷静。

intro.en: Steady takes comparative and verb endings, and builds a noun and a negative form.
intro.cn: steady 加上比较级与动词词尾，并构成名词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: in a firm or even way

items.example: She put a steadying hand on his arm.

definition_en: to take something that belongs to someone else, without permission
core_image: 一只手伸进别人敞开的口袋
scene: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。The thief stole the money from the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 steal 是「偷窃」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。

senses.title: Take without right
senses.definition: to take another person's property without permission
senses.definitionCN: 未经允许拿走他人的财物
senses.example: The thief stole the money from the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。
senses.why: This is the plain physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直接的物理义项。

senses.title: Take ideas
senses.definition: to use someone else's idea or work as if it were your own
senses.definitionCN: 把他人的想法或作品当作自己的使用
senses.example: He stole my idea for the design.
senses.exampleCN: 他剽窃了我的设计方案。
senses.why: An object can be taken, and so can a thought.
senses.whyCN: 物品能被拿走，想法也能。

senses.title: Move quietly
senses.definition: to move somewhere quietly so that no one notices
senses.definitionCN: 悄悄地移动到某处而不被察觉
senses.example: She stole into the room.
senses.why: A thief moves in silence, so the silence itself became the verb.
senses.whyCN: 小偷行动无声，于是「无声」本身也成了动词。

intro.en: Steal goes back to Old English stelan, a strong verb of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: steal 可追溯到古英语 stelan，是日耳曼语来源的强变化动词。

items.en: The root meant to take secretly.
Stelan meant to rob or take by stealth.
items.cn: stelan 意为抢夺或偷偷拿走。

items.en: Stelen kept the strong past form stole.
items.cn: stelen 保留了强变化过去式 stole。

items.en: Steal extended to ideas and quiet movement.
items.cn: steal 扩展到想法与悄悄移动。

items.en: The idiom steal the show named a scene stealer.
items.cn: 习语 steal the show 指抢尽风头的人。

note.en: Steal is compared with look-alike words and with words for taking wrongly.
note.cn: 把 steal 与形近词以及表示不正当拿取的词作比较。

entries.definition: to take from a person by force
to enter a building to steal

normalIntro.en: Steal starts with a hand in a pocket and ends with a silent step through a door.
normalIntro.cn: steal 从一只手伸进口袋开始，以无声的一步进门结束。

normal.en: Someone stole my bike.
Do not steal other people's work.
He stole a glance at the letter.
normal.cn: 他偷偷瞥了一眼那封信。

normal.en: The cat stole into the kitchen.
She stole the show with one song.

abstract.en: What is taken in secret still leaves a trace in the hand.
abstract.cn: 偷偷拿走的东西，仍会在手上留下痕迹。

abstract.en: A stolen idea never fits the thief.
abstract.cn: 偷来的想法，永远不合小偷的身。

abstract.en: Silence is the thief's loudest tool.
abstract.cn: 沉默是小偷最响的工具。

examples.en: The thief stole the money from the counter.
examples.cn: 小偷从柜台后偷走了钱。

examples.en: He stole my idea for the design.
examples.cn: 他剽窃了我的设计方案。

examples.en: She stole into the room.

dict_mnemonic.text: steal 是「偷」，过去式 stole、过去分词 stolen；东西能被偷，想法也能被偷，走路不出声也可以说 steal into。

root: 来自古英语 stelan（偷窃），源于日耳曼语；由秘密拿走财物，引申为盗用想法与悄悄移动。

sensesIntro.en: Steal means to take property, to take credit for an idea, or to move without a sound.
sensesIntro.cn: steal 指拿走财物、窃取想法，或无声地移动。

core.en: A hand closing on what is not its own.
core.cn: 一只手攥住不属于自己的东西。

branches.en: Coins leave a drawer in a closed fist.
branches.cn: 硬币在握紧的拳头里离开抽屉。

branches.en: A speech repeats another person's words.
branches.cn: 一篇演讲重复了别人的话。

branches.en: A door opens without a sound.
branches.cn: 一扇门无声地开了。

branches.en: Property and credit can both be carried off.
branches.cn: 财物与功劳，都能被带走。

branches.en: The quiet step is how the taking begins.
branches.cn: 安静的一步，是拿取的开始。

intro.en: Steal has irregular past forms and builds nouns of theft and secrecy.
intro.cn: steal 有规则外的过去式，并构成表示偷窃与秘密的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_en: the hot gas that water becomes when it boils
core_image: 壶嘴喷出一道翻滚的白汽
scene: 水壶冒出了蒸汽。The kettle gave off steam.
sceneCN: 这里 steam 是「蒸汽」（第 1 个义项）；句意：水壶冒出了蒸汽。

derivatives.zh: 蒸汽弥漫的；潮湿闷热的

senses.title: Boiling water gas
senses.definition: the invisible or white gas produced when water boils
senses.definitionCN: 水沸腾时产生的无色或白色气体
senses.example: The kettle gave off steam.
senses.why: This is the basic physical substance.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物质义项。

senses.title: Cook with steam
senses.definition: to cook food using the heat of steam
senses.definitionCN: 用蒸汽的热量烹制食物
senses.example: She steamed the fish for ten minutes.
senses.why: The gas became a way of cooking.
senses.whyCN: 这种气体成了一种烹饪方式。

senses.title: Energy or anger
senses.definition: the power to keep going, or the pressure of held-in anger
senses.definitionCN: 继续前进的劲头，或压抑的怒气
senses.example: The team ran out of steam.
senses.why: Steam drives engines, so it stands for drive itself.
senses.whyCN: 蒸汽驱动机器，于是它代表驱动力本身。

intro.en: Steam comes from Old English steam, vapour, related to a Germanic root for breath.
intro.cn: steam 来自古英语 steam（汽），与表示呼吸的日耳曼词根相关。

items.en: The root referred to vapour or breath.
Steam meant rising vapour.
Steem also named a hot mist.
Steam power changed industry and travel.
items.cn: 蒸汽动力改变了工业与出行。

items.en: The word grew to mean energy and anger.
items.cn: 这个词又引申出干劲与怒气。

note.en: Steam is compared with look-alike words and with words for vapour and energy.
note.cn: 把 steam 与形近词以及表示蒸汽和劲头的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Steam is water made light, then heat made useful, then pressure made visible.
normalIntro.cn: steam 是变轻的水，是有用的热，也是看得见的压力。

normal.en: Steam rose from the pot.
She steamed the vegetables.
The old train ran on steam.
normal.cn: 那列老火车靠蒸汽行驶。

normal.en: He let off steam after work.
The plan ran out of steam.

abstract.en: Water forgets its weight when it becomes steam.
abstract.cn: 水变成蒸汽时，就忘了自己的重量。

abstract.en: Pressure held too long must find a whistle.
abstract.cn: 压得太久的压力，总要找一个出口。

abstract.en: What drives the wheel also fades into air.
abstract.cn: 推动车轮的东西，也会消散在空气里。

examples.en: The kettle gave off steam.
She steamed the fish for ten minutes.
The team ran out of steam.

dict_mnemonic.text: steam 是烧开水冒出的「蒸汽」，作动词是「蒸」；蒸汽推机器，所以 let off steam 是发泄，run out of steam 是失去动力。

root: 来自古英语 steam（汽），与日耳曼语中表示呼吸的词根相关；由水汽引申为蒸制方式，再引申为驱动力与压抑的情绪。

sensesIntro.en: Steam is the gas of boiling water, the cooking method that uses it, and the drive or anger it suggests.
sensesIntro.cn: steam 是沸水的水汽、用它的烹饪方式，以及它所象征的劲头或怒气。

core.en: White vapour lifting from hot water.
core.cn: 从热水上升起的白色水汽。

branches.en: A lid lifts and a cloud escapes.
branches.cn: 锅盖一掀，一团白汽逸出。

branches.en: A basket of dumplings sits over boiling water.
branches.cn: 一笼饺子架在沸水之上。

branches.en: A piston moves and a long journey begins.
branches.cn: 活塞一动，长途旅程开始。

branches.en: The same vapour softens food and turns wheels.
branches.cn: 同一缕蒸汽，既能蒸软食物，也能转动车轮。

branches.en: Held vapour becomes force, and held anger becomes steam.
branches.cn: 被约束的汽变成力，被压抑的怒也成了蒸汽。

intro.en: Steam takes verb endings and forms adjectives and compounds of steam.
intro.cn: steam 加动词词尾，并构成表示蒸汽的形容词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 那儿放着一杯冒热气的茶。

items.example: The steam engine pulled the train.

definition_en: a ship driven by steam, or a container used for steaming food
core_image: 一艘烟囱冒汽的旧式轮船
scene: 汽船缓缓驶入港口。The steamer sailed slowly into the port.
sceneCN: 这里 steamer 是「汽船」（第 1 个义项）；句意：汽船缓缓驶入港口。

senses.title: Steam ship
senses.definition: a ship powered by a steam engine
senses.definitionCN: 由蒸汽机驱动的船
senses.example: The steamer sailed slowly into the port.
senses.why: This is the historic travel sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是历史上最典型的交通义项。

senses.title: Steaming pot
senses.definition: a pot or basket in which food is cooked by steam
senses.definitionCN: 用蒸汽烹制食物的锅或笼
senses.example: She put the buns in the steamer.
senses.why: The same steam that moves ships cooks food.
senses.whyCN: 推动船只的蒸汽，也用来蒸食物。

senses.title: One who steams
senses.definition: a person or device that steams something
senses.definitionCN: 蒸制某物的人或装置
senses.example: The steamer works by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 那位蒸制师傅在窗边干活。
senses.why: The -er suffix can name a person as well as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -er 既可指物，也可指人。

intro.en: Steamer is steam plus the agent suffix -er, naming a ship or a pot that works by steam.
intro.cn: steamer 是 steam 加施事后缀 -er，指靠蒸汽工作的船或锅。

items.en: Steam named rising vapour.
The suffix -er named a thing that acts.
items.cn: 后缀 -er 指施行动作的物。

items.en: Steamer first named a steam ship.
The word later named a cooking pot.
Travel by steamer faded as engines changed.
items.cn: 随着动力更新，乘汽船出行逐渐减少。

note.en: Steamer is compared with look-alike words and with words for ships and pots.
note.cn: 把 steamer 与形近词以及表示船和锅的词作比较。

entries.definition: a large boat for the sea

normalIntro.en: A steamer is anything that runs on steam, whether it floats or sits on a stove.
normalIntro.cn: steamer 是靠蒸汽运转的东西，不论它漂在水上还是坐在炉上。

normal.en: The steamer crossed the river.
A paddle steamer turned slowly.
normal.cn: 一艘明轮汽船缓缓转向。

normal.en: Steam the fish in a bamboo steamer.
The steamer whistled at the dock.
Lift the lid of the steamer.

abstract.en: One word holds both the sea and the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 一个词里，同时装着大海与厨房。

abstract.en: Steam can carry a thousand people or soften one bun.
abstract.cn: 蒸汽能载千人，也能蒸软一个包子。

abstract.en: The same power looks grand at sea and humble at home.
abstract.cn: 同一种力量，在海上壮观，在家里平凡。

examples.en: The steamer sailed slowly into the port.
She put the buns in the steamer.
A paddle steamer turned slowly.
examples.cn: 一艘明轮汽船缓缓转向。

dict_mnemonic.text: steamer 是 steam 加 -er，靠蒸汽行进的船叫「汽船」，靠蒸汽蒸食的笼叫「蒸笼」；paddle steamer 是明轮汽船。

root: steam（蒸汽）加施事后缀 -er；先指以蒸汽机航行的船，后也指用蒸汽烹食的锅笼。

sensesIntro.en: A steamer is a steam-powered ship, a steaming pot, or one that steams.
sensesIntro.cn: steamer 指蒸汽船、蒸锅，或蒸制者。

core.en: A thing driven by steam.

branches.en: A funnel smokes above a river boat.
branches.cn: 内河船的烟囱冒着烟。

branches.en: A lid lifts over a basket of dumplings.
branches.cn: 蒸笼盖在一笼饺子上被掀开。

branches.en: Hands lift hot food from a rack.
branches.cn: 双手从架子上取下滚烫的食物。

branches.en: The engine and the pot share one source.
branches.cn: 引擎与锅，共用同一个来源。

branches.en: A pot steams only because someone steams.
branches.cn: 锅会冒汽，是因为有人在蒸。

intro.en: Steamer adds -er to steam and takes a plain plural.
intro.cn: steamer 由 steam 加 -er 构成，复数直接加 -s。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A steaming bowl stood by the stove.
items.exampleCN: 炉边放着一碗冒热气的汤。

definition_en: a strong hard metal made from iron and a little carbon
core_image: 一炉烧得通红的钢水缓缓流出
scene: 这座桥用钢建成。The bridge is made of steel.
sceneCN: 这里 steel 是「钢」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥用钢建成。

senses.title: Hard metal
senses.definition: a strong hard metal made by treating iron
senses.definitionCN: 由铁加工而成的坚固金属
senses.example: The bridge is made of steel.
senses.why: This is the material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是材料义项。

senses.title: Blade or tool
senses.definition: a sharp blade or tool made of steel
senses.definitionCN: 用钢制成的锋利刀剑或工具
senses.example: He drew the steel from its sheath.
senses.why: The material stands for the weapon it makes.
senses.whyCN: 材料代指它所制成的武器。

senses.title: Make resolute
senses.definition: to make yourself or someone ready to face something hard
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或某人准备好面对艰难
senses.example: She steeled herself for the news.
senses.exampleCN: 她硬起心肠准备听那个消息。
senses.why: Hardening iron became hardening the mind.
senses.whyCN: 把铁炼硬，引申为把心炼硬。

intro.en: Steel comes from Old English stiele or style, a metal word of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: steel 来自古英语 stiele 或 style，是日耳曼语来源的金属词。

items.en: The root named a hard metal.
items.cn: 该词根指一种坚硬的金属。

items.en: Stiele meant steel as a material.
Steel also named a blade.
Industry made steel the frame of cities.
items.cn: 工业让钢成为城市的骨架。

items.en: The verb grew to mean to harden oneself.
items.cn: 动词义发展出「使自己坚强」。

note.en: Steel is compared with look-alike words and with words for hard materials and resolve.
note.cn: 把 steel 与形近词以及表示坚硬材料与决心的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Steel is iron made harder, a blade made from it, and a mind made like it.
normalIntro.cn: steel 是炼得更硬的铁，是用它打成的刀，也是像它一样硬起来的心。

normal.en: The frame is made of steel.
Stainless steel does not rust.
He has a will of steel.
She steeled herself for the exam.
The steel mill runs all night.

abstract.en: Iron becomes steel by losing what makes it weak.
abstract.cn: 铁去掉使它脆弱的东西，才成为钢。

abstract.en: A hard metal and a hard heart are named alike.
abstract.cn: 坚硬的金属与坚硬的心，被同一个词命名。

abstract.en: What is tempered can bear more than what is soft.
abstract.cn: 经过锤炼的东西，比柔软的承受得更多。

examples.en: The bridge is made of steel.
He drew the steel from its sheath.
She steeled herself for the news.
examples.cn: 她硬起心肠准备听那个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: steel 是「钢」，比铁更硬；stainless steel 是不锈钢；刀剑常用钢制，所以 steel 也可指刀；steel oneself 是使自己坚强。

root: 来自古英语 stiele（钢），源于日耳曼语；由坚硬金属引申为钢制刀剑，再由「炼硬」引申为使人意志坚定。

sensesIntro.en: Steel is the metal, the blade it makes, and the hardness it lends to a person.
sensesIntro.cn: steel 是这种金属、它打成的刀剑，以及它赋予人的坚硬。

core.en: Iron hardened by fire.

branches.en: Red metal pours into a mould.
branches.cn: 通红的金属注入模具。

branches.en: A bright edge slides from a sheath.
branches.cn: 一道亮刃从鞘中滑出。

branches.en: A person breathes once and steps forward.
branches.cn: 一个人吸一口气，迈步向前。

branches.en: The metal and the blade are one material.
branches.cn: 金属与刀，是同一种材料。

branches.en: Hardening metal is the image of hardening the heart.
branches.cn: 炼硬金属，正是炼硬心肠的比喻。

intro.en: Steel takes verb endings and builds adjectives and trade nouns.
intro.cn: steel 加动词词尾，并构成形容词与行业名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: He was steeling for the test.

definition_en: rising or falling sharply, or soaking something in liquid
core_image: 一条几乎直立的陡坡贴着山壁
scene: 山路又窄又陡。The mountain path is narrow and steep.
sceneCN: 这里 steep 是「陡峭的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：山路又窄又陡。

senses.title: Rising sharply
senses.definition: rising or falling at a sharp angle
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的角度上升或下降
senses.example: The mountain path is narrow and steep.
senses.why: This is the shape you see and climb.
senses.whyCN: 这是能看见、能攀爬的形状。

senses.title: Sharp in amount
senses.definition: changing by a large amount in a short time
senses.definitionCN: 在短时间内大幅变化
senses.example: There was a steep rise in prices.
senses.why: A steep slope on a graph looks like a cliff.
senses.whyCN: 图上的陡坡，看起来像悬崖。

senses.title: Soak in liquid
senses.definition: to leave something in liquid so that it takes in flavour or softens
senses.definitionCN: 把某物留在液体中，使其入味或变软
senses.example: She steeped the tea for five minutes.
senses.why: This is an old verb sense that shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这是与形容词同形的古老动词义项。

intro.en: Steep the adjective comes from Old English steap, high and deep; the verb comes from a related soaking sense.
intro.cn: 形容词 steep 来自古英语 steap（高而深），动词义则来自相关的「浸泡」义。

items.en: Steap meant lofty or deep.
Steep described a sharp slope.
A separate verb named soaking.
items.cn: 另有一个动词表示浸泡。

items.en: Steep extended to sharp changes in numbers.
items.cn: steep 扩展到数字的急剧变化。

items.en: Steeped came to mean deeply filled with a quality.
items.cn: steeped 引申为充满某种特质。

note.en: Steep is compared with look-alike words and with words for slopes and sharp change.
note.cn: 把 steep 与形近词以及表示斜坡和剧变的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Steep is a slope you climb with your hands, a graph that jumps, and tea left in hot water.
normalIntro.cn: steep 是要手脚并用的坡，是陡然跳起的曲线，也是泡在热水里的茶。

normal.en: The hill is too steep to climb.
Prices took a steep jump.
Steep the herbs in hot water.
The steep road tired us.
He is steeped in old stories.
normal.cn: 他浸淫于古老的故事中。

abstract.en: What rises too steeply is hard to hold.
abstract.cn: 升得太陡的东西，很难握住。

abstract.en: A steep path shortens the view but lengthens the climb.
abstract.cn: 陡路缩短了视野，却拉长了攀登。

abstract.en: To be steeped in something is to be changed by it.
abstract.cn: 浸在某种东西里，就会被它改变。

examples.en: The mountain path is narrow and steep.
There was a steep rise in prices.
She steeped the tea for five minutes.

dict_mnemonic.text: steep 是「陡的」，山坡陡、曲线陡都可用；作动词是「浸泡」，steep the tea 是泡茶，be steeped in 是浸淫于。

root: 形容词来自古英语 steap（高而深），动词义来自表示浸泡的同形词；由陡坡引申为数字的急剧变化，再由浸泡引申为深受某种影响。

sensesIntro.en: Steep describes a sharp slope, a sharp change, or the act of soaking.
sensesIntro.cn: steep 描述陡坡、剧变，或浸泡的动作。

core.en: A surface that rises almost straight up.

branches.en: A path leans against a cliff.
branches.cn: 一条小路贴着崖壁。

branches.en: A price line jumps like a wall.
branches.cn: 价格曲线像墙一样跳起。

branches.en: Leaves sink slowly in a warm cup.
branches.cn: 叶子在温热的杯里缓缓下沉。

branches.en: A steep slope and a steep rise share one angle.
branches.cn: 陡坡与陡涨，共用同一个角度。

branches.en: What soaks long enough takes on the colour of the water.
branches.cn: 泡得够久的东西，会染上水的颜色。

intro.en: Steep takes comparison, verb endings, and a noun and adverb.
intro.cn: steep 加比较级、动词词尾，并构成名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The cloth is steeped in dye.
The steeple rises above the town.

definition_en: at a sharp angle, or by a large and sudden amount
core_image: 一条曲线像墙一样陡然冲高
scene: 价格急剧上涨。Prices rose steeply.
sceneCN: 这里 steeply 是「急剧地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：价格急剧上涨。

senses.title: At a sharp angle
senses.definition: in a way that rises or falls at a sharp angle
senses.definitionCN: 以很大的角度上升或下降地
senses.example: The path climbs steeply.
senses.why: This is the literal slope sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的坡度义项。

senses.title: By a large amount
senses.definition: by a large and sudden amount
senses.definitionCN: 以很大且突然的幅度
senses.example: Prices rose steeply.
senses.why: A steep line on a chart moves steeply.
senses.whyCN: 图表上陡的线，就是急剧地变化。

senses.title: At a tilt
senses.definition: in a slanted or sloping position
senses.definitionCN: 以倾斜或斜面的姿态
senses.example: The roof slopes steeply to the north.
senses.why: The angle sense narrowed to a tilt.
senses.whyCN: 角度义收窄为倾斜。

intro.en: Steeply is steep plus the adverb ending -ly, built in modern English.
intro.cn: steeply 是 steep 加副词后缀 -ly，在现代英语中构成。

items.en: Steap meant lofty or deep.
Steep named a sharp slope.
The suffix -ly formed the adverb steeply.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 steeply。

items.en: Steeply spread to prices and numbers.
items.cn: steeply 扩展到价格与数字。

items.en: It now describes any sharp change.
items.cn: 它现在描述任何急剧的变化。

note.en: Steeply is compared with look-alike words and with adverbs of sharp change.
note.cn: 把 steeply 与形近词以及表示剧变的副词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Steeply turns an angle into motion: a path climbs, a price jumps, a roof leans.
normalIntro.cn: steeply 把角度变成动作：路在攀升，价在跳涨，屋顶在倾斜。

normal.en: The road rises steeply here.
Sales fell steeply last year.
The hill slopes steeply to the river.
House prices climbed steeply.
The steps go up steeply.

abstract.en: A steep line is a promise and a warning at once.
abstract.cn: 陡峭的曲线，既是承诺也是警告。

abstract.en: What rises steeply can fall the same way.
abstract.cn: 陡升的东西，也能陡落。

abstract.en: The angle shows how little time there is.
abstract.cn: 角度大小，透露出时间还剩多少。

examples.en: Prices rose steeply.
The path climbs steeply.
The roof slopes steeply to the north.

dict_mnemonic.text: steeply 是 steep 加 -ly，本指「陡峭地」，用于价格、数量时常译「急剧地」，rise steeply 与 fall steeply 是最常见搭配。

root: steep（陡的）加副词后缀 -ly；由坡度陡峭引申为数量、价格变动的急剧。

sensesIntro.en: Steeply means at a sharp angle, by a sharp amount, or in a slanted position.
sensesIntro.cn: steeply 指以陡的角度、以急剧的幅度，或以倾斜的姿态。

core.en: A line that climbs like a wall.
core.cn: 一条像墙一样上升的线。

branches.en: A trail leans into a hillside.
branches.cn: 小径斜插进山坡。

branches.en: A number on a screen jumps upward.
branches.cn: 屏幕上的数字向上跳。

branches.en: A roof tilts away from the rain.
branches.cn: 屋顶斜着让雨流走。

branches.en: Both a path and a roof keep the same angle.
branches.cn: 小径与屋顶，保持着同一个角度。

branches.en: A slanted line can also be a risky graph.
branches.cn: 倾斜的线，也可能是一条危险的曲线。

intro.en: Steeply is fixed in form, built from steep and -ly.
intro.cn: steeply 形式固定，由 steep 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The steepness is measured in degrees.
The grain is steeped in water.
The steeple stands on the hill.

definition_en: to control the direction of a vehicle, a ship, or a course of action
core_image: 一只手稳稳握住方向盘
scene: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
sceneCN: 这里 steer 是「驾驶、掌舵」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他小心地把船驶过礁石。

senses.title: Control direction
senses.definition: to control the direction in which a vehicle moves
senses.definitionCN: 控制车辆行进的方向
senses.example: He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。
senses.why: This is the hands-on driving sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是双手操作的驾驶义项。

senses.title: Guide a course
senses.definition: to guide a plan, a discussion, or a group in a direction
senses.definitionCN: 引导计划、讨论或群体朝某方向走
senses.example: She steered the talk back to the main point.
senses.why: A wheel controls a ship, and a hand can control a talk.
senses.whyCN: 方向盘操纵船，手也能操纵谈话。

senses.title: Keep a heading
senses.definition: to keep a ship or aircraft on a chosen course
senses.definitionCN: 使船或飞机保持选定的航向
senses.example: Steer north until you see the light.
senses.exampleCN: 朝北掌舵，直到看见灯塔。
senses.why: The narrow nautical sense of holding a course.
senses.whyCN: 这是保持航向的航海窄义。

intro.en: Steer comes from Old English steoran, to guide or govern, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: steer 来自古英语 steoran（引导、治理），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to guide or direct.
items.cn: 该词根意为引导或指示方向。

items.en: Steoran meant to steer a ship.
Steren widened to guiding any vehicle.
items.cn: steren 扩展到驾驶任何交通工具。

items.en: Steer also meant to guide a course of action.
items.cn: steer 也指引导行动方向。

items.en: Steer clear of became a common phrase.
items.cn: steer clear of 成为常用短语。

note.en: Steer is compared with look-alike words and with words for guiding.
note.cn: 把 steer 与形近词以及表示引导的词作比较。

entries.definition: to find and follow a route

normalIntro.en: Steer is a hand on a wheel, then a hand on a conversation, then a ship held to its course.
normalIntro.cn: steer 是握着方向盘的手，是引导谈话的手，也是把船稳在航线上的手。

normal.en: She steered the car into the lane.
Steer clear of the broken glass.
He steered the ship through the storm.
The teacher steered us to the answer.
normal.cn: 老师引导我们找到答案。

normal.en: Steer the bike with both hands.

abstract.en: Direction is a decision made small, again and again.
abstract.cn: 方向，是一次次微小的决定累积而成。

abstract.en: The hand that steers also chooses what to avoid.
abstract.cn: 掌舵的手，也在选择避开什么。

abstract.en: To guide a talk is to hold a quiet wheel.
abstract.cn: 引导一场谈话，就是握着一只安静的方向盘。

examples.en: He steered the boat carefully past the rocks.
examples.cn: 他小心地把船驶过礁石。

examples.en: She steered the talk back to the main point.
Steer clear of the broken glass.

dict_mnemonic.text: steer 是「掌舵、驾驶」，也指「引导」；steer clear of 是避开；注意它作名词还可指小公牛，但四级主要考动词义。

root: 来自古英语 steoran（引导、治理），源于日耳曼语；由驾船掌舵，扩展到驾驶车辆、引导谈话与行动。

sensesIntro.en: Steer means to drive a vehicle, to hold a ship to its course, or to guide a course of action.
sensesIntro.cn: steer 指驾驶车辆、稳定航向，或引导行动方向。

core.en: A hand on a wheel deciding a direction.
core.cn: 一只手放在轮上，决定方向。

branches.en: A car turns between two white lines.
branches.cn: 一辆车在两道白线间转向。

branches.en: A voice brings a meeting back to the point.
branches.cn: 一个声音把会议拉回主题。

branches.en: A bow holds steady against the night.
branches.cn: 船首在夜色中稳稳朝前。

branches.en: Driving and sailing are the same grip.
branches.cn: 开车与行船，是同一个握法。

branches.en: A talk needs a wheel as much as a road does.
branches.cn: 谈话和道路一样，都需要一只方向盘。

intro.en: Steer takes verb endings and builds nouns of steering and the steersman.
intro.cn: steer 加动词词尾，并构成表示操纵与舵手的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_en: the main stalk of a plant, or to stop something from spreading
core_image: 一朵花挺立在细长的花茎上
scene: 花茎被风吹断了。The flower stem broke in the wind.
sceneCN: 这里 stem 是「茎」（第 1 个义项）；句意：花茎被风吹断了。

senses.title: Plant stalk
senses.definition: the main thin part of a plant that supports leaves or flowers
senses.definitionCN: 植物支撑叶或花的主要细长部分
senses.example: The flower stem broke in the wind.
senses.why: This is the physical plant sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是植物的实体义项。

senses.title: Word base
senses.definition: the part of a word to which endings are added
senses.definitionCN: 词中加词尾的那部分
senses.example: The stem of the word is shown in bold.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词的词干用粗体标出。
senses.why: A plant stem supports growth, and a word stem supports new forms.
senses.whyCN: 植物茎支撑生长，词干支撑新形式。

senses.title: Stop the spread
senses.definition: to stop something from growing or spreading
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某物生长或扩散
senses.example: They tried to stem the flow of water.
senses.why: To hold back the current is to stem it.
senses.whyCN: 挡住水流，就是 stem 它。

senses.title: Come from
senses.definition: to have something as its origin
senses.definitionCN: 以某物为来源
senses.example: The problem stems from poor planning.
senses.why: A branch grows from a stem, so a result stems from a cause.
senses.whyCN: 枝从茎上长出，结果也从原因上长出。

intro.en: Stem comes from Old English stemn, the trunk or stalk of a plant.
intro.cn: stem 来自古英语 stemn，指植物的主干或茎。

items.en: The root named a tree trunk.
Stemn meant the stalk of a plant.
Stem also named the base of a word.
To stem became to check a flow.
items.cn: to stem 变成「挡住水流」。

items.en: Stem from named the source of a result.
items.cn: stem from 指结果的来源。

note.en: Stem is compared with look-alike words and with words for plant parts and origins.
note.cn: 把 stem 与形近词以及表示植物部位和来源的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Stem holds up a flower, then holds up a word, then holds back a flood.
normalIntro.cn: stem 先托起一朵花，再托起一个词，最后挡住一场洪水。

normal.en: Cut the stem just above a leaf.
The word has a Latin stem.
They worked to stem the flood.
The trouble stems from one mistake.
Stem cells can grow into many kinds of cells.
normal.cn: 干细胞能长成多种细胞。

abstract.en: Every branch remembers the stem it left.
abstract.cn: 每一根枝条，都记得它离开的茎。

abstract.en: To stem a flow is to stand still against motion.
abstract.cn: 挡住水流，就是站着不动去对抗流动。

abstract.en: Where a result comes from is where its cure begins.
abstract.cn: 结果来自哪里，解药也从哪里开始。

examples.en: The flower stem broke in the wind.
The problem stems from poor planning.
They tried to stem the flow of water.

dict_mnemonic.text: stem 本义是植物的「茎」，也指单词的「词干」；作动词是「阻止、遏制」，stem from 表示「源于」，两者是四级高频用法。

root: 来自古英语 stemn（茎、树干），源于日耳曼语；由植物的支撑部位引申为词干，再由「挡住流向」引申为遏止，由「枝从茎出」引申为源于。

sensesIntro.en: Stem is a plant stalk, a word base, a check on a flow, or the source a result comes from.
sensesIntro.cn: stem 是植物茎、词干、对流动的遏止，或结果所来自的源头。

core.en: A stalk that holds a plant up.

branches.en: A flower sits at the top of a thin stalk.
branches.cn: 一朵花立在细茎顶端。

branches.en: Endings attach to a bare base.
branches.cn: 词尾接在一个裸词干上。

branches.en: Sandbags hold a river steady.
branches.cn: 沙袋把河水挡住。

branches.en: A problem shows where its root lies.
branches.cn: 问题显出它的根源在哪里。

branches.en: The stalk is both a support and a beginning.
branches.cn: 茎既是支撑，也是开端。

intro.en: Stem takes plural and verb endings, and builds a negative adjective.
intro.cn: stem 加复数与动词词尾，并构成否定形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: had a stem or was checked

items.exampleCN: 干细胞也许能修复组织。

items.example: The fear stems from the past.
They tried to stem the tide.
items.exampleCN: 他们设法遏制这股潮流。

definition_en: a movement of the foot, one action in a process, or to move by putting down a foot
core_image: 一只脚落在下一级台阶上
scene: 她向前迈了一步。She took a step forward.
sceneCN: 这里 step 是「一步」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她向前迈了一步。

senses.title: A movement of the foot
senses.definition: the act of lifting and putting down one foot
senses.definitionCN: 抬起并放下一次脚的动作
senses.example: She took a step forward.
senses.why: This is the basic motion sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的动作义项。

senses.title: One stage in a process
senses.definition: one action in a series that leads to a result
senses.definitionCN: 导向结果的一系列动作中的一步
senses.example: The first step is to make a plan.
senses.why: A walk is a series of steps, and so is a method.
senses.whyCN: 走路是一连串步子，方法也是。

senses.title: A stair tread
senses.definition: a flat surface that forms one level of a stair
senses.definitionCN: 构成楼梯一级的平面
senses.example: Mind the last step.
senses.why: A foot rises from step to step.
senses.whyCN: 脚从一级台阶踏到另一级。

senses.title: Put the foot down
senses.definition: to move by putting a foot down somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 把脚放下并移动
senses.example: He stepped on my foot.
senses.why: The noun of a footfall became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 脚步的名词，转成了动词。

intro.en: Step comes from Old English stæpe, a pace, from the same Germanic family as stair.
intro.cn: step 来自古英语 stæpe（步伐），与 stair 同属日耳曼语族。

items.en: The root named a pace or tread.
Stæpe meant a single pace.
Step also named a stair tread.
Step extended to stages of a process.
items.cn: step 扩展到过程的阶段。

items.en: Phrases like step by step became common.
items.cn: step by step 等短语变得常见。

note.en: Step is compared with look-alike words and with words for movement and stages.
note.cn: 把 step 与形近词以及表示移动和阶段的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Step is one foot, then one stage, then one stair, then the act of treading.
normalIntro.cn: step 是一只脚，是一个阶段，是一级台阶，也是踏下去的动作。

normal.en: Take one step at a time.
The next step is a phone call.
Watch the step at the door.
Do not step on the wet paint.
We moved step by step.

abstract.en: A long road is only many small steps.
abstract.cn: 长路不过是许多小步。

abstract.en: Each step hides the next one.
abstract.cn: 每一步都藏着下一步。

abstract.en: What you step on can also lift you.
abstract.cn: 你踩住的东西，也能把你托起。

examples.en: She took a step forward.
The first step is to make a plan.
He stepped on my foot.

root: 来自古英语 stæpe（步伐），源于日耳曼语，与 stair 同族；由脚的移动引申为过程的阶段与楼梯的踏步。

sensesIntro.en: Step is a foot movement, a stage in a process, a stair, or the act of treading.
sensesIntro.cn: step 是脚的移动、过程的阶段、一级台阶，或踩踏的动作。

core.en: A foot leaving the ground and landing.

branches.en: A shoe moves forward on a road.
branches.cn: 一只鞋在路上向前。

branches.en: A list numbers what comes first.

branches.en: A foot finds a flat stone in a stair.
branches.cn: 脚在楼梯上找到一级平台。

branches.en: A boot presses down on soft ground.
branches.cn: 靴子压进松软的地面。

branches.en: Progress climbs one level at a time.
branches.cn: 进展，一次只上一级。

intro.en: Step takes plural and verb endings and forms compounds of movement and stages.

scene: 她打破了人们对护士的刻板印象。She broke the stereotype of nurses.
sceneCN: 这里 stereotype 是「刻板印象」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她打破了人们对护士的刻板印象。

senses.title: Fixed idea of a group
senses.definition: a fixed general idea that people have about a type of person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人们对某类人或物持有的固定而笼统的看法
senses.example: She broke the stereotype of nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 她打破了人们对护士的刻板印象。

senses.title: Repeated pattern

senses.title: Printing plate

senses.example: The printer kept the old stereotype.

intro.en: Stereotype joins Greek stereos, solid, with type, a printed impression.
intro.cn: stereotype 由希腊语 stereos（坚固的）与 type（印刷的印痕）组合而成。

items.en: Stereos meant solid or firm.

items.en: A stereotype was a fixed printing plate.
items.cn: stereotype 指固定的印刷铅版。

items.en: The word came to mean a fixed idea.
items.cn: 这个词转而指固定的观念。

items.en: It now names unfair general ideas about groups.
items.cn: 现在它指对群体不公平的笼统看法。

note.en: Stereotype is compared with look-alike words and with words for fixed ideas.
note.cn: 把 stereotype 与形近词以及表示固定观念的词作比较。

entries.definition: an unfair opinion formed without knowledge
a simple name put on a group

normalIntro.en: A stereotype is one plate stamped again and again until every face looks the same.
normalIntro.cn: 刻板印象，就是一块版反复压印，直到每张脸看起来都一样。

normal.en: The film plays on an old stereotype.
normal.cn: 这部电影利用了一个老套的成见。

normal.en: Do not judge people by stereotype.
normal.cn: 不要用刻板印象评判人。

normal.en: Gender stereotypes still exist.
normal.cn: 性别刻板印象仍然存在。

normal.en: She does not fit the stereotype.
normal.cn: 她并不符合那个刻板形象。

normal.en: Education can break stereotypes.

abstract.en: A fixed image saves thinking and costs justice.
abstract.cn: 固定的形象省了思考，却赔上了公正。

abstract.en: A plate prints the same face on every page.
abstract.cn: 一块版，会在每一页印出同一张脸。

abstract.en: What repeats too easily stops seeing.
abstract.cn: 过于轻易重复的东西，就不再看得见。

examples.en: She broke the stereotype of nurses.
examples.cn: 她打破了人们对护士的刻板印象。

examples.en: The film avoids the usual stereotype.
examples.cn: 这部电影避开了常见的固定套路。

examples.en: Gender stereotypes still exist.
examples.cn: 性别刻板印象仍然存在。

dict_mnemonic.text: stereotype 原是印刷用的「铅版」，一块版反复印出同样的图，后来引申为人们脑中反复复制的「刻板印象」。

root: 希腊语 stereos（坚固的）加 type（印痕），本指固定铅版；因铅版反复印出同一图案，引申为固定不变的形象与成见。

sensesIntro.en: Stereotype is a fixed idea about a group, a dull repeated pattern, or the printing plate behind the image.
sensesIntro.cn: stereotype 是对某群体的固定看法、乏味的重复模式，或产生这种形象的印版。

core.en: One plate stamping the same picture.
core.cn: 一块版反复印出同一幅画。

branches.en: A whole group is described with one sentence.
branches.cn: 用一个句子描述一整群人。

branches.en: A story repeats the same scene again.
branches.cn: 一个故事又重复同一个场景。

branches.en: A metal plate waits on a press.
branches.cn: 一块金属版等在印刷机上。

branches.en: The printing plate is the image of a fixed mind.
branches.cn: 铅版，正是一颗僵化头脑的形象。

branches.en: What is printed the same way never surprises.
branches.cn: 以同样方式印出来的东西，从不出人意料。

intro.en: Stereotype builds adjectives with -ed and -ical, and a noun with -ing.
intro.cn: stereotype 加 -ed 与 -ical 构成形容词，加 -ing 构成名词。

latinIntro.en: The parts are Greek: stereos, solid, and typos, a stamp.
latinIntro.cn: 其构件来自希腊语：stereos（坚固的）与 typos（印痕）。

items.exampleCN: 刻板化会伤害真实的人。
这是一种刻板化的看法。

definition_en: a thin piece of wood, or to fix something to another surface
core_image: 一根细木棍斜插在泥土里
scene: 他用一根棍子拨火。He stirred the fire with a stick.
sceneCN: 这里 stick 是「棍子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他用一根棍子拨火。

senses.title: Thin piece of wood
senses.definition: a thin rough piece of wood, often broken from a branch
senses.definitionCN: 常从枝条上折下的细而粗糙的木条
senses.example: He stirred the fire with a stick.
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: Fix to a surface
senses.definition: to attach something to a surface with glue or tape
senses.definitionCN: 用胶或胶带把某物附在表面上
senses.example: Stick the photo on the wall.
senses.why: A branch that holds on became a thing that clings.
senses.whyCN: 抓住不放的枝条，变成了黏住的东西。

senses.title: Hold to a choice
senses.definition: to continue with something and refuse to give it up
senses.definitionCN: 继续做某事并拒绝放弃
senses.example: Stick to your plan.
senses.why: To cling to a surface became to cling to a decision.
senses.whyCN: 黏住表面，引申为抓住决定不放。

senses.title: Push a point in
senses.definition: to push a sharp point into something
senses.definitionCN: 把尖头推进某物
senses.example: He stuck the fork into the meat.
senses.why: A pointed stick was the first tool for piercing.
senses.whyCN: 尖棍是最早的穿刺工具。

intro.en: Stick comes from Old English sticca, a twig or peg.
intro.cn: stick 来自古英语 sticca，指细枝或木钉。

items.en: The root named a pointed twig.
Sticca meant a small piece of wood.
Sticken meant to pierce or fasten.
The verb widened to gluing and clinging.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到粘贴与黏附。

items.en: Stick to came to mean holding to a choice.
items.cn: stick to 引申为坚持一个选择。

note.en: Stick is compared with look-alike words and with words for rods and clinging.
note.cn: 把 stick 与形近词以及表示棍棒和黏附的词作比较。

entries.definition: to hurt with a sharp point

normalIntro.en: A stick is a broken branch, then the glue that holds it to a wall, then the will that does not let go.
normalIntro.cn: stick 是一根折下的枝，是把它贴到墙上的胶，也是不肯放手的那股劲。

normal.en: The dog carried a stick.
Stick the note on the door.
Stick to the main road.
The needle stuck in the cloth.
The team stuck together.

abstract.en: What sticks to you can be glue or memory.
abstract.cn: 黏住你的，可能是胶，也可能是记忆。

abstract.en: A thin stick can carry a whole old body.
abstract.cn: 一根细棍，能撑起一整副老去的身体。

abstract.en: To stick to a plan is to keep a promise to yourself.
abstract.cn: 坚持计划，就是对自己守信。

examples.en: He stirred the fire with a stick.
Stick the photo on the wall.
Stick to your plan.

dict_mnemonic.text: stick 是「棍子」，作动词是「粘、贴」，过去式与过去分词都是 stuck；stick to 是坚持，stick out 是伸出，stick together 是团结。

root: 来自古英语 sticca（细枝、木钉），源于日耳曼语；由尖木棍引申为刺入，再由刺入、固定引申为粘贴与坚持。

sensesIntro.en: Stick is a thin branch, an act of attaching, an act of holding to a choice, or a push with a point.
sensesIntro.cn: stick 是细枝、粘附的动作、坚持一个选择，或用尖头刺入。

core.en: A thin branch held in the hand.

branches.en: A dry twig lies by the fire.
branches.cn: 一根干枝放在火边。

branches.en: A corner of paper holds to the wall.
branches.cn: 纸的一角贴在墙上。

branches.en: A person keeps walking the same road.
branches.cn: 一个人继续走同一条路。

branches.en: A point enters soft wood.
branches.cn: 一个尖头扎进软木。

branches.en: The glue and the will both refuse to let go.
branches.cn: 胶与意志，都不肯松手。

intro.en: Stick has irregular past forms and builds nouns and adjectives of clinging.
intro.cn: stick 有规则外的过去式，并构成表示黏附的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.

items.example: She is sticking labels on jars.

definition_en: covered with something that clings, or difficult to deal with
core_image: 糖浆顺着手指慢慢往下滴
scene: 糖浆让她的手指发黏。The syrup made her fingers sticky.
sceneCN: 这里 sticky 是「黏的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：糖浆让她的手指发黏。

senses.title: Tending to cling
senses.definition: covered with a substance that sticks to whatever it touches
senses.definitionCN: 覆有碰到什么就粘住什么的物质
senses.example: The syrup made her fingers sticky.
senses.why: This is the physical sense you feel.
senses.whyCN: 这是能摸到的物理义项。

senses.title: Hot and damp
senses.definition: unpleasantly warm and humid, so that the skin feels damp
senses.definitionCN: 闷热潮湿，皮肤黏腻不适
senses.example: It was a sticky summer evening.

senses.title: Hard to handle
senses.definition: difficult and awkward to deal with
senses.definitionCN: 难以应付、让人为难的
senses.example: We are in a sticky situation.

senses.why: A sticky surface traps the hand, and a sticky problem traps the mind.

intro.en: Sticky is stick plus -y, formed in Middle English from the verb stick.
intro.cn: sticky 是 stick 加 -y，在中古英语中由动词 stick 构成。

items.en: Sticca named a twig.
Sticken meant to pierce or fasten.
Sticky described a clinging surface.
Sticky spread to humid weather.
items.cn: sticky 扩展到潮湿的天气。

items.en: It also named a difficult problem.

note.en: Sticky is compared with look-alike words and with words for clinging and difficulty.
note.cn: 把 sticky 与形近词以及表示黏附和困难的词作比较。

entries.definition: able to stick to a surface

normalIntro.en: Sticky is a hand you cannot wipe dry, air you cannot shake off, and a problem you cannot put down.
normalIntro.cn: sticky 是擦不干的手，是甩不掉的空气，也是放不下的难题。

normal.en: Honey leaves sticky fingers.
Use sticky tape to seal the box.
The weather is hot and sticky.
They are in a sticky situation.
Sticky rice holds together.

abstract.en: Some memories are sticky and will not wipe off.

abstract.en: A sticky problem holds the mind the way glue holds paper.
abstract.cn: 棘手的问题抓住头脑，就像胶抓住纸。

abstract.en: What feels sticky now may be what keeps things together.

examples.en: The syrup made her fingers sticky.
We are in a sticky situation.
examples.cn: 我们处在棘手的局面中。

examples.en: It was a sticky summer evening.

dict_mnemonic.text: sticky 是 stick 加 -y，「黏的」；sticky tape 是胶带，sticky rice 是糯米；天气闷热潮湿也叫 sticky，棘手的局面是 a sticky situation。

root: stick（粘）加形容词后缀 -y；由物理上的黏附，引申为皮肤黏腻的闷热天气与难以脱身的棘手局面。

sensesIntro.en: Sticky means clinging to the touch, damp with heat, or awkward to deal with.
sensesIntro.cn: sticky 指触之黏手、因热而潮湿，或难以应付。

core.en: A surface that holds the finger.

branches.en: Syrup runs down a fingertip.

branches.cn: 夏天衬衫贴在背上。

branches.en: A question has no easy answer.
branches.cn: 一个问题没有轻松的答案。

branches.en: Heat and sugar both make the skin cling.
branches.cn: 热与糖，都会让皮肤发黏。

branches.en: A sticky thing and a sticky problem both refuse to let go.
branches.cn: 黏手的东西与棘手的问题，都不肯放人。

intro.en: Sticky takes comparison and builds a noun and an adverb.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.

definition_zh: 僵硬的；严厉的；生硬的；强烈的

core_image: 一扇久未开合、几乎转不动的旧铰链
scene: 坐久了，他的脖子发僵。His neck was stiff after sitting long.

senses.title: Hard to bend
senses.definition: firm and difficult to bend or move
senses.definitionCN: 坚实而不易弯曲或活动的
senses.example: His neck was stiff after sitting long.
senses.why: This is the physical body sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体的物理义项。

senses.title: Strict and severe
senses.definition: strong and not gentle, as of a rule or punishment
senses.definitionCN: 指规则或惩罚强硬而不宽和的
senses.example: There is a stiff penalty for cheating.
senses.why: A stiff thing does not bend to kindness.
senses.whyCN: 僵硬的东西，不会向仁慈弯下。

senses.title: Formal and awkward
senses.definition: behaving in a formal way that seems cold or unnatural
senses.definitionCN: 举止正式，显得冷淡或不自然
senses.example: He gave a stiff bow.

senses.title: Strong in force
senses.definition: blowing or flowing with great force

senses.example: A stiff wind met us at the door.

intro.en: Stiff comes from Old English stif, rigid or inflexible.
intro.cn: stiff 来自古英语 stif，意为僵直、不弯的。

items.en: The root meant rigid.
Stif described a body that would not bend.
items.cn: stif 描述不肯弯曲的身体。

items.en: Stiff widened to manner and rules.

items.cn: 它开始指强风与激烈的竞争。

items.en: The verb stiffen grew from the adjective.
items.cn: 动词 stiffen 由这个形容词派生。

note.en: Stiff is compared with look-alike words and with words for rigidity and severity.

normalIntro.en: Stiff is a joint that will not turn, a rule that will not soften, and a wind that will not stop.

normal.en: My legs are stiff after the run.
The competition is stiff.

abstract.en: What will not bend may break instead.
abstract.cn: 不肯弯曲的东西，往往会断。

abstract.en: A stiff manner keeps feeling at a distance.

abstract.en: Some strength looks like stiffness until it learns to move.

examples.en: His neck was stiff after sitting long.
There is a stiff penalty for cheating.
He gave a stiff bow.

core.en: A joint that will not turn.

branches.en: A neck refuses to turn after long sitting.

branches.cn: 一条规矩毫不留情地立着。

branches.en: A guest bows without smiling.
branches.cn: 客人鞠躬却不笑。

branches.en: A wind pushes the door hard.
branches.cn: 一阵风用力推门。

senses.title: Coldly

senses.definitionCN: 以冷淡而不友好的方式
senses.example: He replied stiffly and turned away.
senses.exampleCN: 他生硬地回答，然后转身走开。
senses.why: Formality pushed far enough becomes coldness.
senses.whyCN: 拘谨到极点，就成了冷淡。

intro.en: Stiffly is stiff plus -ly, formed in modern English to describe rigid movement or manner.
intro.cn: stiffly 是 stiff 加 -ly，在现代英语中构成，描述僵直的动作或举止。

items.en: Stif meant rigid.
Stiff widened to manner.
The suffix -ly formed stiffly.
It described both bodies and manners.
items.cn: 它同时描述身体与举止。

items.en: It also named a cold way of speaking.
items.cn: 它也指冷淡的说话方式。

note.en: Stiffly is compared with look-alike words and with adverbs of awkward manner.
note.cn: 把 stiffly 与形近词以及表示生硬举止的副词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Stiffly is a body that does not bend, a guest who does not relax, and a voice that does not warm.
normalIntro.cn: stiffly 是不弯的身体，是不放松的客人，也是不升温的声音。

normal.en: He rose stiffly from the chair.
normal.cn: 他僵硬地从椅子上起身。

normal.en: She sat stiffly in the front row.
The soldier stood stiffly at attention.
He answered stiffly and left.
normal.cn: 他生硬地回答后就走了。

normal.en: The old man walked stiffly up the stairs.

abstract.en: A body can be stiff from cold or from pride.
abstract.cn: 身体会因寒冷发僵，也会因骄傲发僵。

abstract.en: What is held too straight cannot bow.
abstract.cn: 挺得太直的东西，弯不下腰。

abstract.en: Stiffness keeps feeling just out of reach.
abstract.cn: 僵硬，让感情总是差一点够不着。

examples.en: He bowed stiffly.
He walked stiffly after the long ride.
examples.cn: 长途乘车后，他僵硬地走着。

examples.en: She sat stiffly by the door.

dict_mnemonic.text: stiffly 是 stiff 加 -ly，指身体「僵硬地」动作，也可指举止「拘谨地」、语气「生硬地」，常与 walk、sit、bow、reply 搭配。

root: stiff（僵硬的）加副词后缀 -ly；由身体的僵直，引申为举止拘谨与言语生硬。

sensesIntro.en: Stiffly means moving without ease, behaving without warmth, or speaking without softness.
sensesIntro.cn: stiffly 指动作不灵活、举止不亲切，或说话不生软。

core.en: A back held straight and still.

branches.en: An old man climbs one stair at a time.
branches.cn: 老人一级一级地爬楼梯。

branches.en: A guest sits far from the cushion.
branches.cn: 客人坐得离靠垫很远。

branches.en: A voice gives a short answer.
branches.cn: 一个声音给出简短的回答。

branches.en: The body sets the tone of the manner.
branches.cn: 身体的状态，决定了举止的基调。

branches.en: Formality at its limit sounds like coldness.
branches.cn: 拘谨到了尽头，听起来就像冷淡。

intro.en: Stiffly is fixed in form, built from stiff and -ly.
intro.cn: stiffly 形式固定，由 stiff 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 脖子僵硬让他动作迟缓。

items.example: A stiff breeze met the boat.
items.exampleCN: 一阵强风迎面吹向小船。

definition_en: continuing up to now, not moving, or even more so
core_image: 一池没有一丝波纹的静水
scene: 他仍然在等她。He is still waiting for her.
sceneCN: 这里 still 是「仍然」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他仍然在等她。

senses.title: Up to now
senses.definition: continuing until the present time, often longer than expected
senses.definitionCN: 持续至今，常比预期更久
senses.example: He is still waiting for her.
senses.why: This is the everyday time sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最日常的时间义项。

senses.title: Not moving
senses.definition: completely quiet and without movement
senses.definitionCN: 完全安静而没有动作
senses.example: The lake was still at dawn.
senses.why: This is the physical calm sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理上的平静义项。

senses.title: Even more
senses.definition: used to make a comparison stronger
senses.definitionCN: 用于加强比较的程度
senses.example: That is still better.
senses.why: Something unchanged in time can add emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 时间上不变的东西，也能用来加强语气。

senses.title: Distilling device
senses.definition: a device used to distil liquid
senses.definitionCN: 用于蒸馏液体的装置
senses.example: The still turned water into vapour.
senses.why: This is a separate noun from the adverb.
senses.whyCN: 这是与副词同形的另一个名词。

intro.en: Still the adjective comes from Old English stille, quiet; the adverb grew from the same word.
intro.cn: 形容词 still 来自古英语 stille（安静），副词义由同一个词发展而来。

items.en: The root meant motionless.
Stille meant quiet and calm.
Still began to mean up to now.
Still also strengthened comparisons.
A separate noun named a distilling pot.

note.en: Still is compared with look-alike words and with words for quiet and for continuation.
note.cn: 把 still 与形近词以及表示安静和持续的词作比较。

entries.definition: the ability to do something well

normalIntro.en: Still is time that will not end, water that will not move, and a comparison pushed one step further.
normalIntro.cn: still 是不肯结束的时间，是不肯流动的水，也是再往前推一步的比较。

normal.en: She is still asleep.
Stand still and do not speak.
The night was still.
It is still colder today.
He kept still behind the door.

abstract.en: What is still has not chosen to move yet.
abstract.cn: 静止的东西，只是还没选择动。

abstract.en: Time that is still is time that is waiting.
abstract.cn: 静止的时间，就是等待的时间。

abstract.en: Quiet water shows the sky more clearly.
abstract.cn: 静水把天空照得更清楚。

examples.en: He is still waiting for her.
The lake was still at dawn.
Stand still and do not speak.

dict_mnemonic.text: still 作副词是「仍然、还」，也可加强比较「更」；作形容词是「静止的、平静的」，stand still 是站着不动；另有名词义「蒸馏器」。

root: 来自古英语 stille（安静、不动），源于日耳曼语；由静止引申为时间上的持续「仍然」，再引申为加强比较的「更」。

sensesIntro.en: Still marks what continues, what does not move, what is even more so, or a distilling pot.
sensesIntro.cn: still 标记持续之事、静止之物、更进一步的程度，或一只蒸馏锅。

core.en: Water with no ripple on it.

branches.en: A lamp burns in a window all night.
branches.cn: 一盏灯整夜亮在窗里。

branches.en: A pond holds the sky without a wave.
branches.cn: 池塘无波地映着天空。

branches.en: One answer is good and another is better.
branches.cn: 一个答案不错，另一个更好。

branches.en: Vapour cools and becomes drops in a pot.
branches.cn: 蒸汽在锅中冷却成滴。

branches.en: What stays calm also stays on.
branches.cn: 保持平静的，也一直在延续。

intro.en: Still takes comparison and builds a noun of quiet.
intro.cn: still 加比较级，并构成表示寂静的名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_en: to make someone or something more active, interested, or developed
core_image: 一粒火星落进干燥的柴堆
scene: 音乐能激发孩子的想象力。Music can stimulate a child's imagination.
sceneCN: 这里 stimulate 是「激发」（第 1 个义项）；句意：音乐能激发孩子的想象力。

senses.title: Arouse interest
senses.definition: to make someone feel interested or eager to think
senses.definitionCN: 使某人产生兴趣或乐于思考
senses.example: Music can stimulate a child's imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐能激发孩子的想象力。
senses.why: This is the mental sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是心智层面的义项。

senses.title: Make more active
senses.definition: to cause growth, activity, or spending to increase
senses.definitionCN: 使增长、活动或消费增加
senses.example: The plan is meant to stimulate the economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划旨在刺激经济。
senses.why: A spark makes a fire grow faster.
senses.whyCN: 火星让火烧得更旺。

senses.title: Excite the body
senses.definition: to make a body or sense organ respond more actively
senses.definitionCN: 使身体或感觉器官更活跃地反应
senses.example: Cold water stimulates the skin.
senses.why: The medical sense of waking a response.
senses.whyCN: 这是唤起反应的生理义项。

intro.en: Stimulate comes from Latin stimulare, to goad, from stimulus, a sharp stick for driving cattle.
intro.cn: stimulate 来自拉丁语 stimulare（驱赶），源于 stimulus（赶牛用的尖刺棒）。

items.en: Stimulus named a goad or prick.
Stimulare meant to prick into action.
Stimulate entered English as a learned verb.
items.cn: stimulate 作为学术动词进入英语。

items.en: It named the waking of body and mind.
It spread to markets and growth.

note.en: Stimulate is compared with look-alike words and with words for arousing and encouraging.
note.cn: 把 stimulate 与形近词以及表示激发和促进的词作比较。

entries.definition: to copy the appearance of something
a substance that makes you more active
to fill someone with an idea

normalIntro.en: Stimulate began as a goad that moved cattle and now moves minds and markets.
normalIntro.cn: stimulate 起初是赶牛的刺棒，如今又能推动头脑与市场。

normal.en: The teacher stimulates discussion.
Coffee stimulates the senses.
Tax cuts may stimulate spending.
Good questions stimulate thought.
Exercise stimulates blood flow.

abstract.en: A small goad moves a large animal.
abstract.cn: 一根小刺棒，能推动一头大牲口。

abstract.en: Interest grows where something first pricks it.
abstract.cn: 兴趣总是从被戳了一下开始生长。

abstract.en: What arouses must then be given room.
abstract.cn: 唤醒之后，还要给它生长的空间。

examples.en: Music can stimulate a child's imagination.
examples.cn: 音乐能激发孩子的想象力。

examples.en: The plan is meant to stimulate the economy.
examples.cn: 这项计划旨在刺激经济。

examples.en: Cold water stimulates the skin.

dict_mnemonic.text: stimulate 来自拉丁语「赶牛刺棒」，所以是「刺激、激发」；stimulate interest 是激发兴趣，stimulate the economy 是刺激经济，名词是 stimulus。

root: 拉丁语 stimulus（赶牛刺棒）加动词词尾；由刺动牲口，引申为激发兴趣、刺激增长与唤起生理反应。

sensesIntro.en: Stimulate means to awake interest, to speed up growth, or to make a body respond.
sensesIntro.cn: stimulate 指唤醒兴趣、加快增长，或使身体产生反应。

core.en: A small point that starts movement.
core.cn: 一个启动运动的小尖点。

branches.en: A song opens a child's mind.
branches.cn: 一首歌打开了孩子的心智。

branches.en: A new road brings trade to a town.
branches.cn: 一条新路给小镇带来贸易。

branches.en: Cold water makes the skin wake up.
branches.cn: 冷水让皮肤一下子醒来。

branches.en: Interest and growth both begin with a push.
branches.cn: 兴趣与增长，都始于一次推动。

branches.en: A body and an economy both need waking.
branches.cn: 身体与经济，都需要被唤醒。

intro.en: Stimulate takes verb endings; its family includes stimulus and stimulation.
intro.cn: stimulate 加动词词尾，其同族词包括 stimulus 与 stimulation。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base stimulus means a goad.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 stimulus 意为刺棒。

items.exampleCN: 那是一场启发人的谈话。

items.example: Light is a stimulus for the eye.

items.exampleCN: 茶里含有温和的兴奋物质。
这消息再次激发了兴趣。

definition_en: to hurt with a sharp point, or a sharp pain caused in this way
core_image: 蜜蜂尾针扎进皮肤的一瞬
scene: 一只蜜蜂蜇了他的手臂。A bee stung his arm.
sceneCN: 这里 sting 是「蜇」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一只蜜蜂蜇了他的手臂。

senses.title: Pierce with a point
senses.definition: to hurt someone with a sharp point, as a bee does
senses.definitionCN: 用尖针刺痛某人，如蜜蜂所为
senses.example: A bee stung his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 一只蜜蜂蜇了他的手臂。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的物理义项。

senses.title: Hurt the feelings
senses.definition: to cause sharp emotional pain
senses.definitionCN: 造成尖锐的情感痛苦
senses.example: The words stung her.
senses.why: A physical prick became an emotional one.
senses.whyCN: 身体的刺，变成了情感的刺。

senses.title: A sharp pain
senses.definition: a sharp burning pain caused by a sting
senses.definitionCN: 由蜇刺造成的尖锐灼痛
senses.example: The sting lasted for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 那股刺痛持续了好几个小时。
senses.why: The action became the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 动作本身变成了感受。

senses.title: A police trap
senses.definition: a secret operation in which police catch criminals
senses.definitionCN: 警方抓捕罪犯的秘密行动
senses.example: The police set up a sting.
senses.why: The trap bites like a hidden needle.
senses.whyCN: 陷阱像藏起来的针一样咬人。

intro.en: Sting comes from Old English stingan, to pierce, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: sting 来自古英语 stingan（刺入），源于日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant to pierce.
Stingan meant to pierce with a point.
Sting named the pain of an insect.
The word extended to wounded feelings.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到受伤的情感。

items.en: A sting became a police trap.
items.cn: a sting 变成警方的诱捕行动。

note.en: Sting is compared with look-alike words and with words for piercing and pain.
note.cn: 把 sting 与形近词以及表示刺入和疼痛的词作比较。

entries.definition: to make a small hole with a point

normalIntro.en: Sting is a needle in the skin, then a needle in the heart, then a trap that waits to bite.
normalIntro.cn: sting 先是扎进皮肤的针，再是扎进心里的针，最后是等着咬人的陷阱。

normal.en: A wasp stung me on the hand.
The sting swelled for a day.
Her reply stung him.
The police ran a sting.
normal.cn: 警方实施了一次诱捕行动。

normal.en: He felt the sting of failure.

abstract.en: The smallest insect can teach the largest animal pain.
abstract.cn: 最小的虫子，也能教最大的动物什么叫痛。

abstract.en: Words can sting longer than a needle.
abstract.cn: 言语的刺痛，比针更久。

abstract.en: A trap is only a sting that waits.
abstract.cn: 陷阱，不过是一根等待中的刺。

examples.en: A bee stung his arm.
examples.cn: 一只蜜蜂蜇了他的手臂。

examples.en: The words stung her.
The police set up a sting.

dict_mnemonic.text: sting 是昆虫「蜇、刺」，过去式与过去分词都是 stung；名词是「蜇伤、刺痛」，言语伤人也可用 sting；a sting operation 是警方的诱捕行动。

root: 来自古英语 stingan（刺入），源于日耳曼语；由昆虫刺人，引申为言语刺痛、痛感本身，以及警方设下的诱捕圈套。

sensesIntro.en: Sting is a point that pierces, the feelings it wounds, the pain it leaves, or a trap that waits.
sensesIntro.cn: sting 是刺入的尖、被它刺伤的情感、留下的痛，或等待中的陷阱。

core.en: A point entering the skin.

branches.en: A bee leaves its point behind.
branches.cn: 蜜蜂把尾针留在皮肤里。

branches.en: A sentence lands and the face changes.
branches.cn: 一句话落下，脸色就变了。

branches.en: A red mark burns for hours.
branches.cn: 一块红痕灼痛好几个小时。

branches.en: Police wait behind a closed door.
branches.cn: 警察在一扇关着的门后等待。

branches.en: A small point and a small word both leave marks.
branches.cn: 一个小尖与一句话，都会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Sting has irregular past forms and builds nouns and adjectives of piercing.
intro.cn: sting 有规则外过去式，并构成表示刺蜇的名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: the sharp part of an insect

definition_en: to move something around in a liquid, or to make a feeling or interest rise
core_image: 一把勺子在热汤里缓缓打圈
scene: 她搅了搅锅里的汤。She stirred the soup in the pot.
sceneCN: 这里 stir 是「搅拌」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她搅了搅锅里的汤。

senses.title: Mix with a spoon
senses.definition: to move a spoon or tool around in food or drink to mix it
senses.definitionCN: 用勺或工具在食物或饮料中转动以混合
senses.example: She stirred the soup in the pot.
senses.why: This is the kitchen sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是厨房里的义项。

senses.title: Wake a feeling
senses.definition: to make a strong feeling or interest begin
senses.definitionCN: 使强烈的感情或兴趣产生
senses.example: The story stirred memories.
senses.why: Stirring a pot raises what lies at the bottom, as words raise feelings.
senses.whyCN: 搅锅会翻起底下的东西，言语也会翻起情感。

senses.title: Move slightly
senses.definition: to move a little from a still position
senses.definitionCN: 从静止状态稍稍移动
senses.example: The leaves did not stir.
senses.why: This is the smallest physical movement.
senses.whyCN: 这是最小的物理动作。

senses.title: Public excitement
senses.definition: a state of great interest or excitement among many people
senses.definitionCN: 众人之间强烈的兴趣或骚动
senses.example: The news caused a stir.
senses.why: A feeling that moved everyone became a public event.
senses.whyCN: 感动众人的情绪，成了一场公共事件。

intro.en: Stir comes from Old English styrian, to move or arouse.
intro.cn: stir 来自古英语 styrian（移动、激起）。

items.en: The root meant to move.
Styrian meant to set in motion.
Stiren named mixing food.
Stir extended to feelings and news.
items.cn: stir 扩展到情感与新闻。

items.en: A stir came to mean public excitement.
items.cn: a stir 指公众的轰动。

note.en: Stir is compared with look-alike words and with words for mixing and arousing.
note.cn: 把 stir 与形近词以及表示搅动和激起的词作比较。

entries.definition: a bright point in the sky
a foot rest on a saddle
to cause a feeling to begin

normalIntro.en: Stir moves a spoon in soup, then moves a feeling in a chest, then moves a whole crowd.
normalIntro.cn: stir 先在汤里转动勺子，再在胸口搅动情感，最后搅动整个人群。

normal.en: Stir the tea before drinking.
The song stirred old memories.
normal.cn: 这首歌激起了旧日回忆。

normal.en: Not a leaf stirred.
The film caused a stir.
Do not stir up trouble.

abstract.en: Whatever settles at the bottom rises when stirred.
abstract.cn: 沉淀在底下的东西，一搅就会浮起。

abstract.en: A small motion can wake a whole room.
abstract.cn: 一个细微的动作，能唤醒一整个房间。

abstract.en: To stir a heart is to change the weather inside.
abstract.cn: 搅动一颗心，就是改变里面的天气。

examples.en: She stirred the soup in the pot.
The story stirred memories.
The news caused a stir.

dict_mnemonic.text: stir 是「搅拌」，引申为「激起」情感或「引起」兴趣；a stir 是「轰动」，stir up trouble 是挑起麻烦，not a leaf stirred 是一点动静都没有。

root: 来自古英语 styrian（使动、激起）；由搅拌食物，引申为搅动情感、引起兴趣与公众的轰动。

sensesIntro.en: Stir means to mix, to wake a feeling, to move a little, or to excite the public.
sensesIntro.cn: stir 指搅拌、激起情感、稍微移动，或引起公众轰动。

core.en: A spoon turning in a pot.

branches.en: Steam rises as the soup turns.
branches.cn: 汤一转，热气就升起。

branches.en: An old song brings back a face.
branches.cn: 一首老歌带回一张脸。

branches.en: A curtain moves once in the wind.
branches.cn: 窗帘被风吹动了一下。

branches.en: A crowd repeats one piece of news.
branches.cn: 人群重复着同一条消息。

branches.en: What is stirred up does not stay at the bottom.
branches.cn: 被搅起来的东西，不会再沉在底下。

intro.en: Stir doubles its final r and builds a noun and an adjective.
intro.cn: stir 双写末尾 r 加词尾，并构成名词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 那是一场激动人心的演讲。

items.meaning: a tool or person that stirs

definition_en: goods kept for sale, a share in a company, or a supply kept for future use
core_image: 货架上整齐码放的存货
scene: 这家店库存不足。The shop is short of stock.
sceneCN: 这里 stock 是「库存」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这家店库存不足。

senses.title: Goods on hand
senses.definition: goods kept in a shop or store ready to be sold
senses.definitionCN: 商店或仓库里备着可供出售的货物
senses.example: The shop is short of stock.
senses.why: This is the everyday shop sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是商店里最日常的义项。

senses.title: Company share
senses.definition: a share in the ownership of a company
senses.definitionCN: 公司所有权中的一份
senses.example: He bought stock in the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了这家公司的股票。
senses.why: A stored value became a tradeable share.
senses.whyCN: 储存的价值，变成了可交易的份额。

senses.title: Keep a supply
senses.definition: to keep goods ready for future use
senses.definitionCN: 为将来使用而备好货物
senses.example: They stock food for winter.
senses.why: The noun of a supply became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 储备的名词，转成了动词。

senses.title: Cooking liquid
senses.definition: a liquid made by cooking meat or vegetables, used as a base
senses.definitionCN: 煮肉或蔬菜得到的液体，用作底汤
senses.example: Add a cup of chicken stock.
senses.why: Stock as a base is another line of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 作为底子的高汤，是另一条词义线。

intro.en: Stock comes from Old English stocc, a tree trunk or post.
intro.cn: stock 来自古英语 stocc，指树干或木桩。

items.en: The root named a trunk or stick.
Stocc meant a tree trunk.
Stock named a supply or base.
Stock came to mean goods and shares.
The cooking sense named a soup base.

note.en: Stock is compared with look-alike words and with words for supplies and shares.
note.cn: 把 stock 与形近词以及表示存货和股份的词作比较。

entries.definition: a soft covering for the foot
a part of a company's value

normalIntro.en: Stock is a trunk that became a store of goods, a share in a firm, and a pot of soup base.
normalIntro.cn: stock 是从树干变成的存货，是公司里的一份股，也是一锅汤底。

normal.en: The item is in stock.
The book is out of stock.
He bought stock in the company.
normal.cn: 他买了这家公司的股票。

normal.en: We stock up before winter.
Add some vegetable stock.

abstract.en: What stands in a warehouse is wealth not yet used.
abstract.cn: 堆在仓库里的，是尚未使用的财富。

abstract.en: A trunk holds branches; a stock holds possibilities.
abstract.cn: 树干撑着枝条，储备撑着可能。

abstract.en: To take stock is to count what you can still use.
abstract.cn: 盘点，就是数一数还能用的东西。

examples.en: The shop is short of stock.
He bought stock in the firm.
examples.cn: 他买了这家公司的股票。

examples.en: Add a cup of chicken stock.

dict_mnemonic.text: stock 由「树干、基础」引申为「库存」和「股票」，也可指汤的「高汤」；in stock 是有货，out of stock 是缺货，take stock of 是评估。

root: 来自古英语 stocc（树干、木桩）；由主干、底子引申为存货与资本股份，另一支引申为汤的底子即高汤。

sensesIntro.en: Stock is goods on hand, a company share, a stored supply, or a cooking base.
sensesIntro.cn: stock 是手头货物、公司股份、储备的供应，或烹饪的高汤底。

core.en: A trunk that holds what grows.

branches.en: Boxes sit on shelves behind a counter.
branches.cn: 箱子码在柜台后的架上。

branches.en: A name is printed on a share certificate.
branches.cn: 一个名字印在股票凭证上。

branches.en: Cans are carried down to a cellar.
branches.cn: 罐头被搬进地窖。

branches.en: Bones simmer slowly in a pot.
branches.cn: 骨头在锅里慢慢炖。

branches.en: Goods and supplies are the same thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 货物与储备，是同一件事的两种看法。

intro.en: Stock takes plural and verb endings and forms compounds of trade and supply.
intro.cn: stock 加复数与动词词尾，并构成表示贸易与供应的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: She hung a stocking by the fire.
items.exampleCN: 她在炉边挂了一只长袜。

items.example: They built a stockpile of grain.

items.meaning: a place where shares are traded
